► Code Blue Cam Merch

On May 10, 2023, police responded to a 911 call about an agitated and intoxicated man at a bar. Upon contact, he resisted, refused orders, and made threats, leading to his arrest. Despite being taken to the jail, he continued to be uncooperative and even threatened to take every single one of their jackets. The situation escalated even further when he was placed in the receiving cell.

Our featured content aims to depict law enforcement interactions, emphasizing education over public shaming or ridicule. In a world filled with misleading conversations about law enforcement, it's crucial to present these interactions within their contexts to inform and educate the public.

jail staff responded to Kevin's cell
after discovering he had tied a shirt around his neck
and seemed to be unconscious.
When they tried to remove him,
the shirt from his neck, Kevin woke up and started swinging at the jail staff.
In response, a taser was deployed on Kevin and he was placed in handcuffs.
During the altercation, Kevin needed deputy in the head, prompting the need for another officer
to take over. Due to his ongoing assaultive and combative behavior, the decision was made
to secure him in the emergency restraint chair. When EMS arrived to evaluate Kevin,
he persistently shouted obscenities at them and refused to answer any questions. At the
time of the incident, it was also discovered Kevin was on an open felony bond in La Crosse County
for making threats to law enforcement with conditions prohibiting alcohol consumption.
Kevin was charged with felony counts of battery threat to an officer, times six,
attempted battery threat to an officer, times two, and bail jumping times two.
He was given a cash bond set at $5,000, but it was later modified to a $10,000 signature bond.
As of November 2003, he was found guilty, but only for three counts of battery threat to an officer.
The remaining charges were dismissed, but read in.
Ultimately, his sentencing hearing is scheduled for February 2024.
